content.content: When the registry's loader reads a record document, the deccy CLI shall check it against `schemas/work.json` with the in-process JSON Schema validator and shall refuse it — naming the record — when that check fails or when the document's `handle` field is not the handle its filename gives, never surfacing it as a record and never passing over it silently.
content.rationale:
This is the read half of the record's conformance rule: the registry's reader checks every document it reads against the record's form and refuses, by name, anything that is not the record its filename says it is. It is `ears` rather than `text` because it fixes a CLI behaviour — a trigger on the read path and the response the loader owes — and not a value, a shape or a stored form; the shape belongs to `wrvsxwmq`, the stored form and its name to `rqtowtqn`, and this sentence reads both without re-deciding either.

Clause by clause. 'the registry's loader reads a record document' takes both halves from `rqtowtqn`: a record is exactly one JSON document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json` and the stored records are enumerated only by scanning that directory, so the only documents a reader can be reading as records are the ones that directory holds. Nothing here re-decides that place, that one-document form or that scan; the trigger presumes them. 'shall check it against `schemas/work.json`' is `wrvsxwmq`, which fixes that schema as the record's form and whose rationale already states the premise this node supplies the reader's half of — every writer and reader of the registry checks the same document shape — so the check is that rule's reader side, not an inspection this node invents. 'with the in-process JSON Schema validator' is `zmmyomyp`, which fixes how documents are checked: the `jsonschema` crate compiling the draft 2020-12 schema in-process, never hand-rolled validation. The sentence names that mechanism and no other, so the 'never by hand-written field inspection' half stays with `zmmyomyp` instead of being restated into a second form here.

'and shall refuse it, naming the record' is the one commitment this sentence adds. `wrvsxwmq` fixes which documents are the record's form and says every reader checks against it; a reader that checked and then read on would have checked without consequence, and `rqtowtqn`'s premise that the directory's documents are the whole record would be false for any document that failed the form and was used anyway. Refusing, never surfacing and never skipping are one response, not three commitments: the document is not a record, so no reader may present it as one, and no reader may silently drop it either. 'naming the record' invents no naming scheme — `rqtowtqn` makes the filename the record's handle, so the record is named by the handle it was read under, and how that name is rendered is not fixed here.

'when that check fails' takes its meaning from `wrvsxwmq` and nothing more: the schema there closes the field set at both levels, fixes the `open`/`landed` enum, the one-string references, the nested workspace and the deliberately unfixed base values, and states that it enforces shape and not meaning — so the refusal fires on shape and never on the validity of what a string points at. That boundary is why this node does not repeat the field list: the list is `wrvsxwmq`'s, and restating it would be a second, driftable copy of the form.

'or when the document's `handle` field is not the handle its filename gives' is the join of `rqtowtqn` and `wrvsxwmq`, and it is why the schema check alone is not enough. `wrvsxwmq` admits any non-empty handle string — the value space of a handle is the minting rule's, so the schema cannot say which handle a given file must carry — while `rqtowtqn` fixes that the filename is the record's handle; a document whose `handle` field names some other handle passes the schema and is still not the record its filename says it is. The comparison is not a new rule about handles: it is `rqtowtqn`'s naming read against the field `wrvsxwmq` requires, and it fixes nothing about how a handle is generated, what it looks like, or whether it is a node id or a change id. That the schema admits a document with a mismatched handle is not a contradiction of `wrvsxwmq`; it is the reason the second ground is stated beside the first. The schema speaks about shape and not meaning, it deliberately leaves the handle's value space to the minting rule, and in the same breath it states that the handle it types is the document's filename stem. Refusing a mismatch therefore applies what `wrvsxwmq` says about that field rather than adding a shape the schema excludes: no document is refused here for a field the schema forbids, and none the form rejects is admitted by this sentence.

'never surfacing it as a record and never passing over it silently' are the two negatives the prerequisites each need. `wrvsxwmq` says the schema is the record's whole form and nothing else, so a document outside that form is not a record and cannot be surfaced as one. `rqtowtqn` gives absence a meaning — a handle the directory does not name is a record that is not there — so a document that is there and fails the check may not be folded into that same meaning: silence would make a present, malformed record indistinguishable from an absent one and would contradict the claim that what the directory holds is what the record is. Refusing while naming the record is the only outcome both prerequisites leave.

Deliberately outside, because each is a separate commitment: the storage form and the directory scan (they are `rqtowtqn`'s, and the trigger presumes them); the field set, the enum, the reference arity, the nested workspace and the unfixed base values (they are `wrvsxwmq`'s); the checking mechanism beyond naming it (it is `zmmyomyp`'s); and the wording of the refusal, what the reading verb prints, its exit status, whether a missing file counts as a refusal, how the schema is located at run time, and the order in which several non-conforming documents are named. A read can refuse a document with none of these settled, and settling any of them would not change what this sentence says.

No clause carries a verdict or evidence: the sentence states what a read does with a document that does not conform, and which document failed is a finding of the read, not content of this node.
